pushA.name: Smith Flat Bench Press
pushA.note: 25 lb bar + 45 a side. Touch chest, no bounce

pushA.name: Mid Cable Fly (on bench)
pushA.note: Hold the stretch behind the torso line

pushA.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
pushA.note: Straight bar behind head, elbows high and close

pullA.name: Chest Supported Row Machine
pullA.note: Lower back stays out of it

pullA.name: Cable Lat Prayer
pullA.note: Straight arms, hinged at hip, shoulders fully overhead

pullA.name: Dumbbell Shrug
pullA.note: 50 lb a hand. Straight up, 1-sec squeeze, no rolling

pullA.name: Cable Reverse Rear Delt Fly
pullA.note: Crossover, swap which arm is on top each set · both arms, alternate which arm crosses on top each set

pullA.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
pullA.note: 30 lb a hand, 45 degree bench, arms behind torso

pullA.name: Single-Arm Cable Hammer Curl
pullA.note: Low pulley, D-handle, elbow pinned · single arm, alternate L/R each set

legsA.name: Smith Machine Squat
legsA.note: Heels elevated on plates, full depth

legsA.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
legsA.note: 25 lb a hand. Upright torso, long stride · single arm, alternate L/R each set

legsA.name: Leg Extension
legsA.note: Load cut from 85, which was failure at 9 reps

legsA.name: Seated Leg Curl
legsA.note: Seated, not lying. Hip flexion means a longer hamstring

legsA.name: Standing Calf Raise (Smith)
legsA.note: Knee straight for gastrocnemius. 2-sec bottom pause

legsA.name: Cable Ab Crunch
legsA.note: Round the spine against the load

pushB.name: Weighted Chest Dips
pushB.note: Bodyweight to start. Forward lean, elbows out, full depth

pushB.name: Flat Dumbbell Bench Press
pushB.note: 40 lb a hand. Accessory now, not max effort. Deep stretch, no lockout

pushB.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
pushB.note: Both dumbbells together, match Push A

pushB.name: Overhead Cable Extension (V-bar)
pushB.note: Bilateral, V-handle. Different implement to Push A's straight bar. Elbows high and close

pullB.name: Weighted Pull-Up
pullB.note: Bodyweight to start. Dead hang, chest to bar

pullB.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
pullB.note: Pull to hip, shoulder blade travels forward at the bottom · single arm, alternate L/R each set

pullB.name: Single-Arm Cable Pulldown
pullB.note: Kneeling, full overhead reach, slight lean away · single arm, alternate L/R each set

pullB.name: Cable Face Pull (two D-handles)
pullB.note: Bilateral, one D-handle a tower at eye height. Pull toward the ears, rotate knuckles back

pullB.name: Preacher Curl
pullB.note: No preacher bench here: set the adjustable bench to about 75 degrees, stand behind it, drape the upper arm over the top pad · single arm, alternate L/R each set

pullB.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
pullB.note: Cable low and behind, elbow behind torso for a full stretch

legsB.name: Dumbbell RDL
legsB.note: 50 lb a hand. Hips back, stop when the hamstrings stop lengthening. Straps ok

legsB.name: Seated Leg Curl
legsB.note: Same machine as Legs A, run lighter and higher-rep

legsB.name: Reverse Hyperextension (flat bench)
legsB.note: Face down on a flat bench, hips at the edge, legs hanging, raise to horizontal. Add a dumbbell between the feet once 15 reps clear

legsB.name: Seated Calf Raise (Smith)
legsB.note: Bench under the bar, bar padded across the KNEES, feet on a plate so the heels drop below. Knee bent for soleus

legsB.name: Hanging Leg Raise
legsB.note: Curl the pelvis up, don't just raise the legs

sections.label: Log quality
why: Captured: RPE logged on 100% of sets, rest timed on most sets, session feel rated, session note written, daily check-in filled in.
This is what makes every other section, and your Body map, accurate rather than guesswork.

advice.label: Progressive overload
advice.text: Most things moved, but Smith Machine Shoulder Press and Dumbbell Lateral Raise went backwards. If that keeps happening, try moving Dumbbell Lateral Raise earlier, while you're still fresh.

advice.label: Rest discipline
advice.text: Nothing past four minutes buys you anything. Set the phone down, count the clock, and start the next set.

advice.label: Rep-range adherence
advice.text: Dropping below the range means the load is winning. Come down slightly and earn the reps back.

advice.label: Fatigue management
advice.text: A collapse like that is nearly always too little rest or too heavy an opening set. Rest longer, or start about 5 lb lighter and hold the reps.
